caseStudies.title: Rebuilding a legacy dashboard for scale
caseStudies.summary: Migrated a monolithic admin panel to a modular Next.js architecture, cutting page load times and engineering onboarding time.
caseStudies.challenge: The client's admin dashboard had grown organically over four years into a single monolithic React application with no clear module boundaries. Every new feature risked regressions elsewhere, deploys took over 20 minutes, and onboarding a new engineer took a month before they could ship safely.
caseStudies.solution: I led a phased migration to a modular Next.js architecture with clear domain boundaries, incrementally rewriting high-traffic modules first while keeping the legacy app live in production. Data access was consolidated behind a typed API layer backed by PostgreSQL, and the deployment pipeline moved to Vercel with preview environments for every PR.
caseStudies.closingParagraph: The client's team now ships multiple times a day with confidence, and the modular structure has supported three major feature launches since handoff without architectural rework.

caseStudies.title: Custom CMS for a multi-brand publisher
caseStudies.summary: Replaced a brittle WordPress setup with a headless CMS purpose-built for editorial speed and brand flexibility.
caseStudies.challenge: Meridian Creative Agency managed editorial content for three distinct brands, each on a separate WordPress instance. Content duplication, plugin conflicts, and slow page loads were causing the editorial team to lose hours every week.
caseStudies.solution: I designed and built a headless CMS with a unified content model supporting multi-brand publishing. Each brand got its own visual theme layer while sharing a single structured content backend. The new system runs on Google Cloud with PostgreSQL, serving content via a typed API to brand-specific Next.js frontends.
caseStudies.closingParagraph: The editorial team now publishes across all three brands from a single interface, with automated cross-posting and brand-specific formatting handled by the system.

caseStudies.title: AI-assisted case management system
caseStudies.summary: Designed and shipped an AI-augmented workflow tool that reduced manual case triage for a field operations team.
caseStudies.challenge: Helios Field Operations handled hundreds of case reports weekly through manual email triage and spreadsheet tracking. Case prioritization was inconsistent and critical cases sometimes waited days before assignment.
caseStudies.solution: I built a case management platform with AI-powered triage that automatically classifies incoming reports, suggests priority levels, and routes cases to the right team members. The system integrates with their existing email workflow and provides a real-time dashboard for supervisors.
caseStudies.closingParagraph: The field team now processes cases in real-time with AI-assisted prioritization, freeing up coordinators to focus on the cases that need human judgment.

caseStudies.title: Operations platform replacing spreadsheets
caseStudies.summary: Built an internal tool consolidating inventory, orders, and reporting into a single reliable system.
caseStudies.challenge: Arterra Boutique ran their entire operations across seven Google Sheets, three email threads, and a WhatsApp group. Order tracking was unreliable, inventory counts diverged from reality, and monthly reporting took a full day of manual compilation.
caseStudies.solution: I built a unified operations platform with real-time inventory tracking, automated order processing, and one-click reporting. The system replaced their spreadsheet workflows with a single web application that the entire team accesses, with role-based permissions and automated notifications.
caseStudies.closingParagraph: The owner now has real-time visibility into operations and the team spends their time on customer-facing work instead of spreadsheet maintenance.
